Another amazing video and the same sort of thing I've been telling people. Not learning AI IF it can be applied to your job, is a sure way to get let go if the company decides to thin the herd. I use it every day to be more efficient, but it can't do my job. How many AI chat bots have ever helped you get the information you needed? I've yet to come across one that did help me with my specific question. Because I'm the person who calls who has a very specific hard to answer question that the AI isn't designed to answer. I just used AI last night to update my shopify page and allow me to sell books direct for the first time. I'm change web code, actual code with the help of AI and I couldn't code a page myself if I tried. Does that mean that web page developers are out of a job? No, just like Maxinomics stated in the video, it will make those web developers more efficient, because me knowing nothing and taking the time to do it myself to save money isn't something the next person may care about. Maybe they have the money to spend on a web developer to design and do everything for them. If I had the money, I'd take that route too. I 100% agree with this video. AI is a tool... a very GOOD tool for jobs that require time consuming tasks.

Yes, in SOME fields, it will take away the tedious tasks. In others, all it leaves is the tedium. Eg trucking. There will always be a need for humans to do "the last mile." But the long, enjoyable drive was what made the last mile tolerable. Now AI will take all that, leaving nothing but "last miles" for a growing pool of out-of-work drivers.

So I guess we are just imagining the tens of thousands of layoffs happening everywhere or the entry level tech jobs that are disappearing, the internships drying up. Those "tasks" no one wants to do are how humans learn. Despite nail guns every carpenter worth there weight had to also learn how to use a hammer and you cant build a house with just nail guns, you have to be able to swing a hammer. The problem with AI is its not making the nail gun better, its trying to replace the need to learn to hammer, its trying to automate that process and then the humans that needed to learn how that hammer works, to feel the resistance of the wood as they hammered to learn things about the materials they will be working with that no book could ever teach them. This is the experience AI is removing, Just like your pyramid example, that was the job of an entry level freelancer or someone just trying to enter the space who is trying to build a portfolio, now they don't get the chance and will never learn and are stuck at some job they hate because AI took there chance to learn. That being said I do believe there is great potential in AI, but it has to be regulated extensively, it cant be used as a shortcut for everything, or a replacement for our creativity, imagination, or the hard work it takes to learn something. Instead we should be focused on using it to replace the must brutal and dangerous jobs required to make the world go round, like the precious metal miners, or any other job extracting hazardous material from far off, hard to oversee places. The main goal of AI right now should have nothing to do with profit and everything to do with making the world a safer, and less hazardous place for the people who inhabit it. The other side of it is who gets to profit from it, AI was made possible because of all of us and therefore all of us should be the beneficiaries of it.

This really resonates with me and I think other people as well. Had the same thing happen to me when I was in undergrad. I remember calling my mom one night and just sobbing after I had failed one of my classes, unsure of what to do and if CS was the right major for me. I think a lot of people in this major are like that, and that's because the learning curve for programming is steep and daunting. Once you get over that curve, you learn things at a faster pace, but things still take a lot of time, practice and discipline. I literally fail all the time still; I look at lee215's solution on LC and go how the hell did he do that? And I wish I had other people's brains. But holy f*ck if I compared myself to what I was years ago, my past self would be asking my current self the same question. It's hard not to compare yourself with others, especially in the face of constant rejections, but once you hit rock bottom there's only one way you can go, and that's back up.
